{{Quote|Stay on target!|Davish Krail, as Gold Five|<ref name="anh" />}}
'''Davish Krail''', known by his comrades as "'''Pops'''," was a veteran [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who flew for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. He had been flying for nearly twenty years before joining the Alliance, and served at the organization's [[Dantooine base/Legends|base]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] alongside his old friend [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Garven Dreis]]. He was given command of a Y-wing [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] at some stage, but eventually served under [[Jon Vander/Legends|Jon Vander]] in [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron]].

When the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] entered the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Krail was amongst the pilots sent by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] to [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destroy]] the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. He accompanied Vander and [[Tiree/Legends|Tiree]] in the first attack on the station's [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|exhaust port]], but during the trench run, his allies were gunned down by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]. Aborting his run, Krail too was shot down by the Dark Lord, but not before alerting Dreis, [[Red Leader/Legends|commander]] of the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing fighter]] unit [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]], to the threat.

==Biography==
===Rebel===
Since at least [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="popscard">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Pops}}</ref> the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="anh" /> Davish Krail flew [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]],<ref name="popscard" /> and over the course of his career, he fought in many engagements. He had kept the same helmet over the years, and eventually it was battered to a state that it was no longer useful. One of Krail's friends during his earlier flying years was [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Garven Dreis]],<ref name="anhn">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> who flew with the [[Virujansi Rarefied Air Cavalry/Legends|Rarefied Air Cavalry]].<ref name="vt">{{StoryCite|story=Vader Tech|book=Vader: The Ultimate Guide}}</ref> By the time of his joining the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], he was a veteran [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]],<ref name="popscard" /> and was given command of a [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighter]] [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] at the Alliance's [[Dantooine base/Legends|base]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]].<ref name="gold3card">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Gold 3}}</ref> Also serving at the base was Krail's old friend, Dreis.<ref name="r1card">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Red 1}}</ref>

With younger pilots such as [[Ryle Torsyn/Legends|Ryle Torsyn]] under his command,<ref name="gold3card" /> Krail eventually came to be known as "Pops," since he was in his elder years while serving the Alliance.<ref name="anhn" /> He was later assigned to [[Jon Vander/Legends|Jon Vander's]] Y-wing [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron]], and flew as Vander's [[Wingmate/Legends|wingman]] under the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] of "[[Gold Five/Legends|Gold 5]]."<ref name="popscard" /> Krail personally supervised all maintenance and repairs on his Y-wing.<ref name="gold5card">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Gold 5}}</ref> He and his comrades were transferred<ref name="gold3card" /> when the Alliance was later forced to abandon the Dantooine base and relocate to the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="anh" />

===The Battle of Yavin===
{{Quote|Gold Five to Red Leader! Lost Tiree; lost Dutch!''"<br />"''I copy, Gold Leader.''"<br />"''They came from behind!|Davish Krail and [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Garven Dreis]]|<ref name="anh" />}}
In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the Alliance prepared to [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|strike at and destroy]] the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]]. [[Death Star plans/Legends|Technical readouts]] to the station had been delivered to the Great Temple by [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], allowing [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] to devise a plan of attack. It was the intent of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] to have snubfighters approach the station, fly down one of its surface trenches, and fire [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] down a two-meter-wide exhaust shaft. The warheads would hopefully go down the shaft into the battlestation's main [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]], and ultimately destroy the superweapon.<ref name="anh" /> Since the Y-wings were best suited for bombing runs,<ref name="xwa">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''</ref> Gold Squadron was selected to make the first attack against the exhaust port. However, in bringing the plans to [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]] 4, Organa and her companions had been tracked by the Imperials, and as a result they had brought the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] itself to the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]].<ref name="anh" />

Left with little choice but to begin his attack immediately while the Death Star bore down on Yavin 4, Dodonna launched Dreis' [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]], Vander's Gold Squadron,<ref name="anh" /> [[Merrick Simms]]' [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Blue Squadron]],<ref name="ra">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]''</ref> and [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Green Squadron]] against the station.<ref name="anhn" /> Krail flew on Vander's wing as usual, and as the Alliance fighters neared the station, the veteran pilot followed his commander toward the target shaft. Meanwhile, Dreis and his "Red Boys" drew the battlestation's defensive fire away from Gold Squadron. Eventually, the Imperials launched [[Black Squadron (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Black Squadron]], composed of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]], to deal with the Alliance fighters. While TIEs fought with Red Squadron, Vander, Krail, and [[Tiree/Legends|Tiree]] began their attack run on the Death Star's [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|exhaust port]].<ref name="anh" />

[[File:KrailTrenchRun-ANH.jpg|thumb|left|205px|Vander's, Krail's, and Tiree's Y-wing fighters in the trench run]]
As the trio began their descent into the trench, Vander marked the exhaust port's location. When in the trench itself, he ordered Krail and Tiree to switch all their power to their front [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]]. As they were beset by cannon fire from turrets within the trench, Vander requested that Krail estimate just how many defensive turrets the trench had. The veteran completed the task while hurtling down the trench, and supposed that there were approximately twenty in total, spread between the station's surface and its towers. As they neared the exhaust port, Vander switched to his [[Targeting computer/Legends|targeting computer]] before the defensive fire abruptly stopped. Krail suggested that they switch to rear deflector shields, and advised his comrades to be wary of possible enemy fighter attacks from behind.<ref name="anh" />

Sure enough, Vander immediately identified three enemy fighters headed for their position. One of them was a [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]], piloted by [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].<ref name="anh" /> Since they could not fend off the enemy craft and attack the objective simultaneously, the trio were forced to doggedly continue toward the exhaust port, in spite of the threat.<ref name="anhn" /> The new arrivals entered the trench behind the trio, and Vader quickly shot down Tiree. Vander began panicking, and protested that the trench was too small, restricting his evasive options. Krail continually beseeched Vander to focus on his objective, but the younger man continued to fret, urging the veteran to move away from his fighter and loosen up formation. The requests were made in vain, however, as Vader swiftly dispatched Vander as well.<ref name="anh" />

[[File:KrailKaput-ANH.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Krail's Y-wing is destroyed, killing him in the process.]]
The loss of [[Gold Leader/Legends|Gold Leader]] proved to be too much for even an experienced veteran like Krail.<ref name="anhn" /> Now alone in the trench with Vader on his tail, Krail pulled out of the run and contacted Dreis, informing the [[Red Leader/Legends|Red Squadron commander]] of Gold Squadron's failure.<ref name="anh" /> With his last breath he informed Red Leader that Vader and his wingmen had attacked them from behind, before the Dark Lord shot down and killed the veteran. Dreis would also be killed by Vader shortly thereafter, but Red Squadron pilot [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] eventually succeeded in destroying the station to win the day for the Alliance.<ref name="anh" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|How many guns do you think, Gold Five?''"<br />"''Say about twenty guns; some on the surface, some on the towers.|Jon Vander and Davish Krail assess the Death Star's defenses|<ref name="anh" />}}
An experienced man and fighter pilot, Davish Krail would retain a determined demeanor while others would frantically panic. When Tiree perished under Vader's guns during the Battle of Yavin, Vander began to lose sight of the objective as he feared for his own safety. Admonishingly, Krail, who was the older man, tried to keep his superior dedicated to his task. Although he failed in that act, he did use his final moments to aid his allies with intelligence. Over his years of service, he had kept the same battered helmet,<ref name="anhn" /> although he did not wear the chinstrap when going into battle.<ref name="anh" /> Krail had [[Color/Legends|graying]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]].<ref name="Movie Heroes" />

==Behind the scenes==
Davish Krail was portrayed by [[Graham Ashley]] in [[George Lucas]]' [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. He had technically first appeared in [[Alan Dean Foster]]'s [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of the film. In the novel, he was identified as "Pops." The novel had also identified what was Gold Squadron in the film as Red Squadron, and hence, the character was identified as "Red Five," which was the callsign given to Luke Skywalker in the film. The "Red Five" designation was also used in ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''. Krail's character in the film was referred to as "Gold Five," with the exception of one instance in which Garven Dreis addresses him as "Gold Leader." One of Gold Five's lines in the [[Star Wars (radio)|radio drama]] adaptation of the film was spoken by Tiree in the film itself.

The character was given the name of "Davish Krail" in the [[1995]] "[[Premiere Limited]]" set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]]. In [[1998]], however, [[Jude Watson]] would identify "Gold Five" as [[Talos Merkin]] in ''[[Star Wars Journal: Captive to Evil]]'', which was initially assumed by fans to be a mistake. Many years later, [[Jason Fry]] revealed that he considered Merkin to be one of the candidates for the role of [[Red Twelve/Legends|Red Twelve]] in ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'', thus indicating him to be, in fact, a separate character.<ref name="Notes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24614452839/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-10|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 10}}</ref>

There is a reference to Krail in the video game [[Wikipedia:Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos|''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'']]. When destroyed, the Dwarven Gyrocopter unit will utter "They came from behind!" before disintegrating, in a very similar way to Gold Five in the movie. Blizzard Entertainment staff has confirmed that this is one of many intentional references/homages to Lucas' ''Star Wars'' universe.
